headline: Authorization succeeded; no broker repair needed
summary: The alert coincided with a successful prompted keepalive for account slot 1 at 02:30:21 Eastern on October 12. Both accounts subsequently passed bounded metadata-only checks. The broker remained available throughout the observed checks; no software repair or service restart was warranted.
cause: Authorization: slot 1 completed its keepalive with exit 0 and status ok_prompted in 4.21 seconds. The previous recorded prompt was 43,486 seconds earlier (12 hours 4 minutes 46 seconds), consistent with ordinary authorization renewal; the exact revocation trigger is not established. The preceding 30-minute keepalive window contained ten successful calls and no recorded failure or lock transition. Parser/watchdog: the app and console were unlocked, the heartbeat advanced, no active fault episode was recorded, and deployed broker/keepalive hashes matched current sources. The snapshot category authorization_or_unknown is a broad fallback, not independent proof of a failure.
resolution: No implementation change, candidate patch, installation, authentication wake or retry loop was needed. The existing service and its authorization were preserved. Only sanitized incident evidence and the README incident guidance were added. The first-click gate remained false; a verified no-change conclusion may settle without it.
verification: All 44 focused Python tests passed across broker transport, keepalive, recovery, activation and agent guidance. All three Node test files for dispatch, settlement and archive completed successfully. Synthetic coverage includes rotated/stale lock logs, startup not implying lock, locked/unknown-console suppression, prompt/queue distinctions, one-time recovery wake and release gating. Source/deployed hashes, running keepalive hash, build stamp and bundle signature matched. Two real vault-list metadata calls through /Users/taylor/dotfiles/bin/op returned exit 0 in 0.621 and 0.732 seconds with stdout/stderr discarded. Final readback confirmed advancing heartbeat, broker PID 1051/session 1051/PTY /dev/ttys000 and keepalive PID 1055 unchanged. See artifacts/python-tests.json, node-tests.json, deployed-hashes.json, metadata-smoke.json and final-status.json.
activation: The existing broker and keepalive remain running with the verified current sources. Nothing is staged and no activation command or restart is required. This incident is ready for commit/publication and deferred self-archive after the completed turn.
limitations: The exact reason for authorization renewal was not proven. Successful CLI metadata access does not independently establish which physical authentication interaction occurred. No Touch ID/macOS prompt was approved by this agent; no physical notification click, UI test or credential read was performed. The deferred archive helper must independently verify archival after turn completion; scheduling alone is not proof.
docs: Reviewed src/onepassword/README.md, src/onepassword/agent-contract.md and src/onepassword/autofixes/AGENTS.md. Updated README.md with this incident and the distinction between successful prompted authorization and parser/watchdog faults. The shared contract and autofix policy remain accurate and unchanged, so guidance synchronization was unnecessary.
